paper: P1 (worked example); P2 ledger record; P3 factor list
extends: sigec campaign (ledger seq 46, adopted SiC contrast = density edge per ledger seq 61)
question: Which of H, D, He, B and P, in the physical form each takes in sintered Si-Ge-C, lowers the lattice thermal conductivity enough to act as a design lever, and does any of them change the recipe (x_Ge, carbon as few-nm SiC) or the Ge saving?

forms.B, P: substitutional point defect, mass and size (Tamura), n = 1e19..3e20 cm^-3, as in the nano campaign
forms.H, D (isolated): interstitial point defect: an added mass m_X at a site, Gamma = c (m_X/mbar)^2 (lower bound); upper bound adds a local-strain term eps*delta^2 with eps = 39 and delta = 0.3 (bond-centre relaxation, deliberately generous); n = 1e18..1e20 cm^-3. H and D differ only in mass, so the H-vs-D difference isolates the isotope effect.
forms.He (isolated): interstitial point defect, mass-only and the same generous strain bound, n = 1e18..1e20 cm^-3
forms.He or H (cavities): implanted He (or H) plus anneal forms nanocavities; modelled as spherical voids with the same inclusion cross-section as SiC (Rayleigh with lam2 -> geometric limit 2 pi R^2), lam2 bracketed by 1 (one contrast term) and 4 (density and stiffness terms both -1, Rayleigh weight 1+3), plus the Maxwell-Eucken porosity factor (1-phi)/(1+phi/2); R = 2.5, 5, 10, 25 nm; phi = 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3 vol%

grid.x_Ge: nano campaign host grid (committed almaBTE modes)

reference_point: x = 0.2, d_eff = 0.3 um, 300 K and 1100 K; SiC comparison at equal volume fraction (1 at% C as SiC = 1.0 vol%), density-edge contrast

predictions.PrL1: isolated H and D at <= 1e20 cm^-3 change kappa_L by less than 1% (mass-only) at the reference point, all T
predictions.PrL2: isolated H, D or He change kappa_L by less than 5% even at the generous strain bound
predictions.PrL3: the H-vs-D difference in kappa_L is below 0.5% of kappa_L at every grid point (no thermal isotope lever)
predictions.PrL4: at equal volume fraction (1 vol%) and radius (5 nm), He cavities lower kappa_L more than SiC (density edge), both T
predictions.PrL5: 1 vol% of 5 nm cavities saves at least 25% Ge at equal kappa_L versus carbon-free x = 0.2 (300 K)
predictions.PrL6: SiC (1 at% C, 5 nm) plus cavities (1 vol%, 5 nm) together give less than the sum of their separate reductions
predictions.PrL7: B and P stay below 1% change of kappa_L on top of the SiC recipe (x = 0.2..0.5, 1e19..1e20 cm^-3)

decision_rule.lever: a dopant form is a thermal design lever if it changes kappa_L by >= 5% at the reference point
decision_rule.inert: below 1%: recorded as thermally inert; it stays in the factor list only for electrical reasons
decision_rule.recipe: if any lever changes the screening pick (argmin over x, carbon, dopant form) the pick is corrected on the ledger; otherwise the recipe is strengthened

out_of_scope_stated_in_advance: electrical effects (B-H passivation, carrier scattering by cavities), which decide zT
retention: whether H, D or He stay in the solid at 1100 K service; cavity coarsening kinetics
local vibrational modes of Si-H / Si-D (far above the Si phonon band; no resonant term modelled)
